candidates.title: Muscle abnormalities worsen after post-exertional malaise in long COVID
candidates.why: Definitive muscle-biopsy PEM study: long-COVID patients biopsied before/after a provoking exercise challenge; post-PEM mitochondrial (succinate dehydrogenase) dysfunction, glycolytic shift, fiber-type shift, capillary/amyloid changes, local tissue necrosis. Most mechanistically direct PEM-bioenergetics evidence in long COVID.

candidates.title: WASF3 disrupts mitochondrial respiration and may mediate exercise intolerance in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome
candidates.why: The Hwang 2023 PNAS WASF3 paper named in the task: ER-stress-induced WASF3 impairs mitochondrial supercomplex assembly and respiration in ME/CFS muscle/cells, a candidate molecular mechanism for exercise intolerance with a tractable target.

candidates.title: Metabolic features of chronic fatigue syndrome
candidates.why: Seminal hypometabolic 'dauer' metabolomics paper: broad downregulation across sphingolipid, phospholipid, purine, microbiome and mitochondrial pathways resembling a conserved cell-danger/torpor response; the founding metabolomic framing for the bioenergetic-PEM hypothesis.

candidates.title: Exercise Pathophysiology in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2
candidates.why: Invasive CPET (Systrom group) directly addressing the deconditioning-vs-pathology debate: ME/CFS and PASC show preload failure and impaired peripheral O2 extraction at the tissue/mitochondrial level rather than a deconditioning-only ceiling. Key counter-explanation arbiter.

candidates.title: Plasma metabolomics reveals disrupted response and recovery following maximal exercise in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome
candidates.why: Provoked-state metabolomics: maximal exercise yields a disrupted metabolite response and failed recovery trajectory in ME/CFS vs controls, the metabolomic signature of PEM and a candidate provoked biomarker.

candidates.title: Inability of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome patients to reproduce VO2peak indicates functional impairment
candidates.why: Foundational 2-day CPET result: day-2 failure to reproduce VO2/workload at peak and at threshold, the objective physiological PEM signature underpinning the 2-day protocol.

candidates.title: Single-cell transcriptomics of the immune system in ME/CFS at baseline and following symptom provocation
candidates.why: Post-exertional single-cell immune transcriptomics: maps how CPET provocation reshapes immune-cell programs (platelet/megakaryocyte, classical monocyte, T/NK changes) in ME/CFS, linking PEM to the immune arm of the bioenergetic model.

candidates.title: Metabolic profiling indicates impaired pyruvate dehydrogenase function in myalgic encephalopathy/chronic fatigue syndrome
candidates.why: Pyruvate-dehydrogenase-block hypothesis: amino-acid/metabolite pattern implies a PDH bottleneck shunting metabolism away from oxidative ATP, a specific and testable bioenergetic lesion.

candidates.title: An Isolated Complex V Inefficiency and Dysregulated Mitochondrial Function in Immortalized Lymphocytes from ME/CFS Patients
candidates.why: Seahorse/respirometry ME/CFS work named in the task: isolated Complex V inefficiency with compensatory hyperactivation of respiration in patient lymphoblasts.

candidates.title: Substrate utilisation of cultured skeletal muscle cells in patients with CFS
candidates.why: Tomas (Newton group) respirometry on cultured myotubes: altered substrate utilisation and AMPK/glucose-uptake response, the muscle-cell counterpart to the lymphoblast bioenergetic findings.

candidates.title: Cardiopulmonary and metabolic responses during a 2-day CPET in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: translating reduced oxygen consumption to impairment status to treatment considerations
candidates.why: Recent large 2-day CPET dataset translating the day-2 oxygen-consumption deficit into impairment classification, updating Keller2014 with clinical-endpoint framing.

candidates.title: Functional and Morphological Differences of Muscle Mitochondria in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and Post-COVID Syndrome
candidates.why: Directly compares muscle mitochondrial function/morphology between ME/CFS and post-COVID, testing the shared-vs-trigger-specific bioenergetic question (q0011 core).

candidates.title: Key Pathophysiological Role of Skeletal Muscle Disturbance in Post COVID and Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS): Accumulated Evidence
candidates.venue: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
candidates.why: Authoritative review consolidating skeletal-muscle bioenergetic/microvascular disturbance as a shared post-COVID/ME-CFS lesion; good orienting synthesis for the muscle arm.

candidates.title: A systematic review of mitochondrial abnormalities in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome/systemic exertion intolerance disease
candidates.why: Systematic review documenting the historical inconsistency of ME/CFS mitochondrial findings across assays, the key evidence-maturity caveat for q0011.

candidates.title: Diagnostic sensitivity of 2-day cardiopulmonary exercise testing in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome
candidates.why: Quantifies the diagnostic sensitivity/test characteristics of the 2-day CPET, needed to judge it as a candidate objective PEM endpoint.

candidates.title: Cardiopulmonary Exercise Test Methodology for Assessing Exertion Intolerance in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome
candidates.why: Methods/standardization reference for the 2-day CPET protocol (Workwell group), the procedural backbone for reproducible provoked testing.

candidates.title: Decreased oxygen extraction during cardiopulmonary exercise test in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome
candidates.why: Reduced peripheral oxygen extraction during CPET, evidence the lesion is at tissue/mitochondrial O2 utilisation rather than central cardiac output, bearing on deconditioning debate.

candidates.title: Whole blood human transcriptome and virome analysis of ME/CFS patients experiencing post-exertional malaise following cardiopulmonary exercise testing
candidates.why: Earlier post-CPET whole-blood transcriptomic/virome readout of PEM; complements Vu2024 single-cell data on exertion-driven molecular change.

candidates.title: Exertional Exhaustion (Post-Exertional Malaise, PEM) Evaluated by the Effects of Exercise on Cerebrospinal Fluid Metabolomics-Lipidomics and Serine Pathway in ME/CFS
candidates.why: CSF metabolomics/lipidomics of provoked PEM implicating serine/one-carbon pathway, the CNS-bioenergetic dimension of PEM.

candidates.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in long COVID: mechanisms, consequences, and potential therapeutic approaches
candidates.why: Heavily cited review of long-COVID mitochondrial mechanisms (redox, NAD+, ATP) and therapeutic candidates; orienting synthesis for the long-COVID bioenergetic arm.

candidates.title: The Occurrence of Hyperactivated Platelets and Fibrinaloid Microclots in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS)
candidates.why: Microclots/hyperactivated platelets in ME/CFS, the oxygen-delivery-impairment mechanism linking thromboinflammation to tissue hypoxia and bioenergetic failure (overlaps thromboinflammation topic).

candidates.title: Post-Exertional Malaise Is Associated with Hypermetabolism, Hypoacetylation and Purine Metabolism Deregulation in ME/CFS Cases
candidates.why: Foundational metabolomic work the OMF itaconate-shunt hypothesis (Phair/Davis) builds on; the closest peer-reviewed anchor for the itaconate-shunt sub-area, which otherwise exists only as conference/OMF material.

candidates.title: Microvascular Capillary and Precapillary Cardiovascular Disturbances Strongly Interact to Severely Affect Tissue Perfusion and Mitochondrial Function in ME/CFS Evolving from the Post COVID-19 Syndrome
candidates.why: Mechanistic model coupling microvascular perfusion failure to mitochondrial dysfunction; integrative but hypothesis-heavy.

candidates.title: Chronotropic Intolerance: An Overlooked Determinant of Symptoms and Activity Limitation in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome?
candidates.why: Davenport (named in task): chronotropic intolerance as a CPET-derived autonomic determinant of activity limitation.

candidates.title: Extracellular vesicle proteomics uncovers energy metabolism, complement system, and endoplasmic reticulum stress response dysregulation postexercise in males with ME/CFS
candidates.why: Post-exercise EV proteomics implicating energy metabolism + ER stress (links to WASF3/ER-stress axis); small, single-sex.

candidates.title: Skeletal muscle adaptations and post-exertional malaise in long COVID
candidates.why: Review by the Appelman2024 muscle-biopsy group consolidating the long-COVID muscle-adaptation/PEM story.

candidates.title: Towards an understanding of physical activity-induced post-exertional malaise: insights into microvascular alterations and immunometabolic interactions in post-COVID condition and ME/CFS
candidates.why: Integrative PEM mechanism review (microvascular + immunometabolic) spanning both conditions; useful framing, not primary data.

candidates.title: Validity of 2-Day Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing in Male Patients with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome
candidates.why: Replication of 2-day CPET day-2 deficit in males; low-impact venue but supports reproducibility.

candidates.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Coenzyme Q10 Supplementation in Post-Viral Fatigue Syndrome: An Overview
candidates.why: CoQ10/redox-NAD+ therapeutic-angle review; relevant to the redox sub-area but interventionist and lower-evidence.

candidates.title: Metabolomic and immune alterations in long COVID patients with chronic fatigue syndrome
candidates.why: Long-COVID-with-CFS metabolomics + immune profiling; cross-trigger metabolomic overlap evidence.

candidates.title: A SWATH-MS analysis of ME/CFS peripheral blood mononuclear cell proteomes reveals mitochondrial dysfunction
candidates.why: PBMC proteomics showing mitochondrial-pathway dysregulation; complements Peppercorn2023 (already in corpus).

candidates.title: Oxidative stress is a shared characteristic of ME/CFS and Long COVID
candidates.why: Recent PNAS oxidative-stress / redox cross-condition comparison; relevant to redox/NAD+ sub-area.
